sections.name: Revenant
sections.card:
Summary: A flying demon with a jetpack. Once it has locked on, it fires volleys of homing missiles from its rocket launchers. Its claw swipe is the only other attack, and it hits much less hard.
Looks like: Glowing green eyes, cybernetic parts around the head and neck, and rocket launchers detailed so that they look like mouths.
Tips: It will dash out of the way of your shots too.

sections.name: Mancubus
sections.card:
Summary: A large, slow heavy demon with 3,500 health, or 490 while staggered. Its arm cannons throw fireballs from a distance. Up close it switches to two flamethrowers and a blast that leaves harmful energy lingering on the floor.
Weak points: Break its arm cannons and its attacks do far less damage, and the flamethrowers stop working altogether. A chainsaw or glory kill to the chest blows it up: big demons nearby take damage and stagger, and small ones can die.
Looks like: Two small greenish eyes, armour plating on its body, and a bare, glowing yellow organ that looks like a heart sitting in its chest.
Tips: Stay at range and use heavy weapons, because its flamethrowers and ground blast hurt a lot up close. The rocket launcher suits it since it is too slow to dodge rockets, and the ballista's speed and damage take cannons off from far away. The heavy cannon's precision bolt scope can snipe cannons from across the arena, but check behind you while scoped. Do not let it pin you in a corner: it is big, and it hits hard at close range.

sections.name: Pinky
sections.card:
Summary: An armoured demon whose main attack is a charge. It has 1,000 health, but takes bonus damage from hits on its tail and from the blood punch.
Weak points: Its tail is completely unarmoured, so hits there do the most damage. A direct blood punch kills it on the spot, whichever side it lands on.
Tips: Double-jump or dash to avoid the charge, and lure it into a wall: it gets stunned long enough for you to hit the tail. Freezing it with an ice bomb keeps it from turning. Sustained fire wears down its front armour, and the very strongest weapons (the ballista's destroyer blade mod, for one) go straight through it.

sections.name: Baron of Hell
sections.card:
Summary: A fast, aggressive demon that wields two flaming blades. It can survive a single direct BFG hit.
Looks like: Grey-brown skin the colour of ash, burning eyes, flesh glowing under the skin like hot coals, and magma in place of blood. It wields two flaming blades, and its shots are orange and red.
Tips: Keep your distance, just beyond the reach of its leap, and hot-swap among your heaviest weapons; the ballista, rocket launcher and super shotgun all work. A blood punch knocks it back and makes it easier to stun. Keeping the chaingun firing can hold off its attacks.

sections.name: Dread knight
sections.card:
Summary: A Hell knight rebuilt with cybernetics and an energy blade on each arm. The blades give it more reach up close and let it fling a wave of energy at range. It has more health than a Hell knight, but the same ways of beating a Hell knight all work on it as well.
Tips: Watch for it crossing its arms: that is the start of the energy wave, so you can dodge it. When it leaps and slams down, it leaves harmful energy spread around itself, so keep clear. The rocket launcher's lock-on burst staggers it with a single use. The ballista and super shotgun make it flinch, and if you swap between all three it never gets a turn to attack.

sections.name: Prowler
sections.card:
Summary: A sneaky purple demon with 1,000 health, or 250 while staggered. It teleports next to or behind you, then pounces with a quick melee attack that does heavy damage.
Weak points: One direct ballista hit staggers it at once, and a super shotgun blast from point-blank range kills it outright. An ice bomb pins it in place so it cannot teleport away.
Looks like: A humanoid demon built like an imp but bigger, with long claws, purple skin and bony plates sticking out of its back. Its face has three eyes clustered together in the middle, and its jaw is in three sections.
Tips: It is most dangerous when other demons are around, since they keep you busy and you may not notice it before it strikes. If it feels threatened it teleports away and sets up another ambush. From a distance, it may fire quick purple bolts of energy while it runs at you.

sections.name: Carcass
sections.card:
Summary: A cyborg demon with 1,200 health, or 240 while staggered, so it is fairly fragile. It fires ring-shaped lasers, sends shockwaves running along the floor from its arm blaster, and raises a force field wall that shields itself or other demons.
Weak points: Its force field is highly resistant to explosives, but a plasma rifle shot or a blood punch breaks it easily. A shot to the circle marked on the tank at its back kills it instantly.
Looks like: A robot body with three insect-like legs carries the upper half of a zombie human. Its right arm carries a built-in blaster, and a dish sits at its waist.
Tips: It usually puts the shield up in front of staggered demons so you cannot glory kill them with ease, and also when you are holding the rocket launcher or sticky bombs. When the shield is right beside the carcass, detonate it with the plasma rifle; otherwise a pair of ballista shots or super shotgun blasts is enough. Up close, it spins around and lands two hits one after the other.

sections.name: Pain elemental
sections.card:
Summary: A flying demon that spawns lost souls and attacks with them. They come as quick homing shots, as mines left on the ground, or in a barrage of three. Its health is about the same as a baron of Hell's.
Weak points: The rocket launcher's lock-on burst mod is a good answer, since it cannot dodge guided missiles: two volleys that connect kill it. As with other flying demons, the ballista does bonus damage to it.
Looks like: A brown, round demon that flies, with one big red eye, a pair of long black horns, muscular arms with large claws, and a wide mouth with eight mandibles.
Tips: Shoot when it is busy or on the verge of attacking, because it air-dashes away if it sees a weapon aimed at it. It can also push its lost souls in front of your shots to use as shields. The mines hit harder than a direct attack and splash even on a near miss, so tight spaces are risky. Do not use the meat hook on it: you may latch onto one of its lost souls instead and be left somewhere dangerous.

sections.name: Tyrant
sections.card:
Summary: A cybernetic demon that fires missiles from an arm cannon. It is a major enemy that keeps coming back, often two at a time in later levels. One direct BFG hit is not enough to kill it.
Weak points: It turns slowly, so circle behind it with a dash and hit it there. Its own dash is weak, so the meat hook and super shotgun work as long as you keep to its back. The Crucible kills it in one hit.
Looks like: A two-legged demon with a cybernetic right leg, a weapon in place of its left arm, and an energy blade projecting from its right arm. Its ribs show, tubing fills its belly where intestines would be, and a mechanical-looking spine has vertebrae poking out of the flesh. Each side of its bulbous head carries two big horns, and its eyes are yellowish-white.
Tips: When it has no line of sight to you it fires a barrage of missiles, and glowing runes show where they will land. Once it spots you it pauses to aim, which is your chance to attack. An unmistakable triple beep warns of its laser cannon: either duck behind cover or dash right at the end to spoil its aim. Up close it swings the blade, or uses it for shockwaves.

sections.name: Ballista
sections.card:
Summary: A heavy energy-beam weapon that fires in a straight line. It shoots slowly, but each shot hits harder than any other weapon's before mods, and no other weapon is as accurate. You get it after coming back from Doom Hunter Base.
Uses: Its beam passes through demons it kills, so it handles a row of lined-up fodder. Each shot costs 25 cells, so save it for weak points that neither the heavy cannon nor the combat shotgun's sticky bombs can reach, for a hot-swap combo with another weapon, or for flying enemies like the pain elemental, which takes bonus damage from it.
Tips: Arbalest mod: after a short charge it fires a dart that lodges in an enemy and blows up a moment later. It slows you while active and must be reloaded after every shot. Destroyer Blade mod: after charging, it shoots a broad, horizontal blast that pierces a cluster of enemies and costs 50 cells a shot. The recoil is strong enough to give you extra air time or push you across an arena, and with every ammo upgrade a full load is only ten shots, fewer than any other weapon.

sections.name: Heavy cannon
sections.card:
Summary: An all-round automatic rifle with two mods, Precision Bolt and Micro Missiles. You get it early on, once the second demon fight of the Hell on Earth level is over.
Uses: It is dependable at middle to long range, and two body shots take down most fodder. On its own it struggles against tougher enemies, so use it from a distance to add damage alongside other weapons. The Precision Bolt scope makes shots more accurate and hits weak spots harder, enough to wreck an arachnotron's cannon or a revenant's rocket launchers. Micro Missiles do area damage without the self-damage you risk when firing the rocket launcher up close.
Tips: Precision Bolt is the best mod for Maykr drones, because killing one with a headshot makes it drop plenty of resources. The cannon is hitscan: the result of each shot is fixed the moment you fire. That suits quick fodder at long range, which the plasma rifle cannot hit. Micro Missiles home in slightly, launch as many as six missiles per salvo that explode on impact, and need a reload between salvos.

sections.name: Plasma rifle
sections.card:
Summary: A fast energy rifle that fires small, bright blue orbs of plasma. You first find it in Exultia, right after the trans-dimensional portal.
Uses: Energy shields, such as those of the shield soldier and the carcass, overload under plasma fire and explode, badly hurting whoever holds them and damaging nearby enemies. It also turns off a Doom hunter's body shield so it can be hurt, and wears down an armoured baron's armour. It cannot touch the magic shields of the arch-vile and the marauder.
Tips: Enemies hit by several orbs in quick succession burst in an energy blast. That helps against crowds but can ruin a glory kill. The Microwave Beam mod is a short-range beam that locks onto an enemy, holds it still and keeps damaging it while the beam lasts. Nothing else you carry can kill a spirit, so keep it stocked when a demon is possessed. The Heat Blast mod fires a cone out in front of the weapon, and you charge it by firing the rifle normally.

sections.name: Ice bomb
sections.card:
Summary: A bomb fired from the Praetor suit's shoulder launcher that freezes its target solid. The frozen demon cannot move or fight back, and it breaks apart once it has taken enough damage. You choose it over the frag grenade with a toggle button.
Uses: Freeze a target to hit it while it is stuck, to stop a dangerous enemy attacking, or to get away when you are surrounded. Whiplashes move fast, so the ice bomb is especially recommended against them. It also pins a pinky or spectre so you can go for its weak back end. You cannot glory kill a frozen enemy.
Tips: How long a freeze lasts depends on the enemy: 4 seconds for most fodder; 2 for pinkies, revenants and cacodemons; 1.5 for mancubi and barons of Hell; 1 for tyrants. Once the bomb is upgraded, each of those lasts longer. It does nothing to demons that a spirit has possessed or a screecher has buffed. The cooldown is 45 seconds, or 35 with the faster cooldown suit upgrade.

sections.name: Flame belch
sections.card:
Summary: A quick blast of flame from the Praetor suit's shoulder launcher that lights enemies on fire. You find it at the Fortress of Doom, once Hell on Earth is finished, and it is ready to use whichever grenade type you have selected.
Uses: Enemies that are on fire take bonus damage and drop armour shards, and one that dies while burning drops more. It is your main way to get armour in a fight, and it works next to the chainsaw and glory kills as part of the combat loop. Sweep left and right as you fire to catch a group.
Tips: The combat shotgun and super shotgun give extra armour when they kill a burning enemy. The cooldown is 25 seconds, or 12.5 with the Quickdraw Belch suit upgrade. Sentinel crystals buy three upgrades: that shorter cooldown, a longer burn on heavy and super heavy demons, and armour that drops out faster.

sections.name: Blood punch
sections.card:
Summary: A powerful melee strike that you charge up by getting glory kills. Its shockwave also damages enemies around the one you hit. You first pick it up as a glowing artifact in Exultia.
Uses: Pinkies and spectres die instantly, or at least take severe damage, and tougher monsters take heavy damage. It breaks enemy shields, including the arch-vile's magical one. It is very likely to damage a weak point, up to wrecking a cyber-mancubus's armour entirely.
Tips: It uses no ammo, but it needs charging first: two glory kills make one charge, and you can hold only one at a time. It gets three automatic upgrades later in the game: a stronger shockwave, an instant charge from one glory kill on a heavy demon, and room for a second charge. Against a big group of fodder, freeze them, burn them with the flame belch, then blood punch one to take your health and armour to full.
